# Ironwood Books

Ironwood Books is a one-person press. Evan Paliotta writes books for his son and shares them with any family that finds them useful: picture books for young children and a life-wisdom guide for teenagers, all built around ideas that have held up for a long time. Every ebook is free. Paperbacks are sold at cost-plus on Amazon.

## Books

- [The Adventures of the Curious Kid](https://ironwoodbooks.com/books/the-adventures-of-the-curious-kid): A rhyming picture book for ages 4-8 about a boy who spends one day exploring everything, including the parts that feel scary. Book 1 of the Curious Kid series.
- [The Curious Kid Meets Aristotle](https://ironwoodbooks.com/books/the-curious-kid-meets-aristotle): A rhyming picture book for ages 4-8. A papyrus scroll sends the Curious Kid to ancient Athens, where Aristotle teaches him the Golden Mean: not too much, not too little. Book 2 of the Curious Kid series.
- [The Curious Kid Meets Lao Tzu](https://ironwoodbooks.com/books/the-curious-kid-meets-lao-tzu): A rhyming picture book for ages 4-8. Green bamboo slips pull the Curious Kid to a bamboo grove, where a still sage shows him that opposites lean on each other — light needs dark, song needs quiet, and an empty cup is useful because of the space inside it. Book 3 of the Curious Kid series.
- [The Ways of the World](https://ironwoodbooks.com/books/the-ways-of-the-world): A short nonfiction guide for teenagers (ages 14+) on power, money, human nature, and building a life worth living, written by a father for his son.

## Guides

- [/guides](https://ironwoodbooks.com/guides): Articles on raising kids who think for themselves, drawing on ideas from the books above. Includes a philosophy books for kids list, a how-to-think books list, a how-to-talk-to-your-kid-about-philosophy guide, an explainer on Aristotle's Golden Mean, and a books-for-reluctant-teen-readers list.
